newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia Adria to replace aircraft by end 1998.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia Adria to replace aircraft by end 1998.

text.p: Slovenia's only airline Adria Airways said on Monday it planned to replace all or most of its aircraft by the end of 1998.
"We plan to replace our planes by smaller and technologically more appropriate aircraft but have not yet decided what planes to buy," Adria's spokeswoman Ljerka Zupancic told Reuters.

Currently Adria, which is owned by Slovenia's state-owned Bank Rehabilitation Agency, has a fleet of seven aircraft comprising three Airbus A320, two McDonnell-Douglas DC9 and two De Havilland Canada Dash 7 planes.
Slavko Jamnik, head of the agency, told daily Republika that Adria would most probably look for aircraft among some seven-year-old Boeing and Canadair planes.
He said the company hoped to replace aircraft at a profit so no extra capital would be needed but pointed out the government would have to give approve each replacement.
New planes will have between 50 and 120 seats, while Adria's Airbuses have 168 seats each.

By replacing its fleet Adria hopes to improve its load factor which was 54 percent in the first 11 months of 1996, unchanged from the same period of 1995. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
